name: Casa do Infante
description: A medieval building by the river that served as the royal customs house. Prince Henry the Navigator is said to have been born here in 1394.

name: Factory House
places: Factory House, Rua do Infante Dom Henrique
description: An 18th-century Georgian building where British port wine shippers have met and dined since the 1790s.

name: Porto Cathedral
description: The Romanesque cathedral on the hill above the old town, begun in the 12th century and later remodeled in Baroque style.

name: Avenida dos Aliados
description: The city’s grand central avenue and square, lined with granite buildings and closed at the top by the City Hall tower.

name: Port wine lodges
places: Port wine lodges, Cais de Gaia
description: Riverside cellars in Vila Nova de Gaia, across the Douro from Porto, where port wine is aged in barrels before shipping.

name: Luís I Bridge
description: A two-level iron arch bridge over the Douro, opened in 1886, linking Porto with Vila Nova de Gaia.

name: Estádio do Dragão
description: The home stadium of FC Porto, the city’s main football club, opened in 2003 for the Euro 2004 championship.

name: Casa da Música
description: An angular concert hall designed by the Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas and opened in 2005.
